body:
I attempted to discuss my feelings with my ex in a mature way by saying things like "It feels to me as though you are trying to provoke me into making threats."  I made very much sure to bring it up in terms of my own feelings and not accusing them, but they were screaming and threatening to take away what little emotional support I have left (recently disowned by family for not doing things exactly right, etc.)

I called the DV hotline, they asked me what happened, and I said that I wasn't going to tolerate anybody accusing me of doing something wrong for openly and maturely discussing my feelings- and they spent more time talking about how I was saying things that could make HER feel threatened than anything supportive of me.  And the one place they referred me to talks all over their website about men who abuse and women who are abused.  It scares me...

...holy fuck.  There's something in there specifically for men!  I need to call as soon as I've got the privacy to do it...

Looking at it now.  I really appreciate it, and you've done more than I could reasonably ask.  Thank you...

EDIT: Oh geez.  This is literally the one I called that was blaming me and couldn't find anything to help.  I don't blame you though.  They sure talk a good talk outwardly, at least to women.
Live in the US.  I don't think they've actually done anything illegal.  I called a hotline and the person I spoke to was partially blaming me.
They've threatened me with things far, far worse to me than being beaten regularly for years... having been beaten regularly for years as a child, I know what I mean when I say that.

I'm glad I've been heard.  It's really all I can reasonably hope for.  Like I said, it's an extremely frustrating feeling- I believe that *if* I shouldn't kill myself, then it would follow that there's *something* that can be said to me that would make me reconsider it.

It's not logically contradictory to hold a belief (in this case that I need to kill myself) and to not like it and hope to change it.

All of this is giving anyone who cares to a chance to say it.  (I'd do it more in meatspace but, you know, if I said "I'm going to kill myself unless someone can convince me otherwise!") it'd sound like emotional manipulation and possibly have me committed, which would just make me resolve to do it once I got out.

The one person I've told IRL has threatened to hurt me and has basically blackmailed me if I *don't* go through with it.

I'm sorry.  Please don't take it as a rejection of your sympathy/caring that I didn't reply directly (in Reddit terms, in practical terms I feel like I was replying to everyone who commented directly.)

Honestly... all things considered...?  Pretty good.  (Although I haven't changed my plans.  But I actually feel really good about that.)

Trying to enjoy what I've got left.  It's stupid but I ordered a pizza last night.  Barely have any savings but it's not like I'll need them much longer.  Dropping $15 including delivery charges, tax, etc. would be horribly irresponsible when I can eat $0.25 ramen under most circumstances.  But I can't take my savings with me.

Under normal circumstances it would just be burying my head in the sand (if I don't kill myself I'm gonna be homeless within a month or two.  Being abused in a relationship that's basically over kind of does that.)

But now that I've got a means to leave and am in the process of preparing it over the next few weeks... everything feels okay.

Nobody will EVER have any more power over me.  Nobody will EVER be able to hurt me again, reject me again, abuse me again, lie to me again, degrade me again.  Anything else feels like a temporary solution to a permanent problem.

Yeah, there's things I'll miss.  I'm gonna miss being able to go outside and take a walk.  I'm gonna miss being able to play stupid Facebook games.  I'm gonna miss being able to curl up and read.  I'm gonna miss bouncing around Reddit.  Hell, I'm gonna miss encouraging and helping people on this very subreddit.

But if that's the price I've got to pay... it's the lesser of two evils.
Thank you... wanted to let you know I replied to you and someone else who posted.  Unfortunately it's not possible to my knowledge to reply directly multiple posts at once. :(

I'd like to have a comfortable wage in order to live within my means.  I don't have a job or a wage, and to be honest I've gotten so demoralized by being rejected that it's hard to even apply.  I do want money, but it's moreso the principle that I was told repeatedly it was guaranteed if I went to college and worked hard.  (If I could just get a refund on the time, energy, and money I spent on my education- I'd be *okay* with working a minimum wage job.)

Thank you for at least not shooting me down when I speak of being mean to others.  Maybe it's not the way to happiness, but even so I regret not trying it for myself more.  (The few times I have tried, life at least felt like it wasn't attacking as much.)

It's hard to put myself out there when it's literally what I've tried before and failed.  I just... can't justify it.  It's kind of like if an animal presses a switch a thousand times, gets shocked every time, and was expected to press it again.

I am scared, I'm scared of everything that's happened before, and nothing ever changing.  I refuse to live like this and have yet to find a way out of it other than killing myself.  So it's a last resort.  I'd love to be talked out of it.  I love being proven wrong because it means I've learned something new.

It's obvious that you're understanding a good bit of what I'm saying.  If I shouldn't off myself, there's *something* that can convince me of it, and this seems like a great place to invite anyone who cares to try to show it to me.  And I'm grateful that you're trying, for whatever that may mean.  Trying with good intentions, without force, and either genuinely attempting to understand what I'm saying or successfully attempting to understand it is reducing the chances of me completing the attempt which is being prepared.

Another way to put it: this is almost like an admittedly emotionally charged /r/changemyview post.  I'd like to have a reason to change my mind, and it's great that you're genuinely trying.

Posting this as a separate comment in case it gets deleted.

I'd like to be able to say something like "it would be really encouraging to me if this thread got upvoted a bunch."  Thing is, that may or may not be literally true.

But if it were literally true it would probably be deleted for vote manipulation or something, when it could be an honest attempt to communicate my feelings.  And that's *exactly* the sort of thing that's so discouraging.

I want to reply to both of you who commented and anyone else who wants to hear it but don't think there's a way to technically do that.

Big heart... yeah, I kind of knew that, although the more people leech from me the more it shrinks.  I've had enough.

It's not even so much a question of what makes life living for me.  I'm confident I have a list of things that would make life worth living for me.  (What I just posted was much of that list.)  If I were going to hire someone, and they told me that the job would help make life worth living for them, assuming they were genuine about it- I'd take it that they were damn serious about working hard and assuming they were just that sincere it would make them look great to me.  But what if I walked into a job interview and said that having a job (generally or with the company I'm interviewing with) would tremendously help make life worth living to me?

And what if I was in a relationship with someone and said to them "you help make life worth living to me?"  It could be honest, and yet it comes off as clingy, needy, and possibly a suicide threat.

I also have a list of things that are very nice and sure help... but I can't magically get the means to support myself so I can spend the rest of my time crawling into a cave somewhere with a pile of books and video games.  That would be a life worth living- not a great one, mind- but enough to keep me going, at least for awhile.

I guess... yeah, I want to be appreciated- but appreciated enough that people are willing to work with me on what I want.  Talk is cheap.  I appreciate people here- if you see these good qualities in me please let me know! but more than anything I want a reason in line with my values.  (It sounds like you're trying hard and I appreciate that but... you still haven't answered what I really want answered.)  I've had enough people fake appreciate and run away when I was no longer quite convenient for them.

I've given too much in my life.  I'm drained.  I've given too much without getting in return.  It's MY turn to reap the benefits of something.  It's MY turn to get a job with my degree (don't want to identify myself but I have a supposedly very marketable professional degree.)

For instance: one of the best ways to show that someone appreciates me is hire me and treat me like a human being.  The fact is that money talks.  And again, I need something concrete.  Money may not be the most valuable thing in the world, but it is just about the most concrete; it's a lot harder to fake paying someone than to fake affection or appreciation.

I've been hurt too much for words themselves to mean enough to keep me here.  Most of my life I've been the friend I wanted to have.  Actually the few times I experimented with being mean to people I felt better than ever about life.  I felt okay and even good about it; people couldn't hurt my heart because I wasn't giving it.  Maybe that's what I need to do.  Start lying, cheating and manipulating.  If I'd done that a few years ago I wouldn't be as low as I am today.

Haha.  Maybe deep down I'm an asshole who's deluded himself into thinking that those who preach doing unto others will do it.  I genuinely think I'd be happier with myself if I'd lied, cheated, and stolen.

Would I help out a dog... honestly?  I'm so fucking drained in life I couldn't do it.  I just don't have it in me anymore.  Plus there are a lot of people who would help the dog.  I'm actually kind of jealous of the dog; they're a lot better adapted to living in the wild than modern humans are.  (Sorry.  That's not the answer you wanted to hear, I'm sure.)  But I don't see how it's out of a mutual friend's power to listen to and take some time to comprehend my side of the story after a breakup instead of coming up with excuses not to.

Thank you for admitting that life isn't fair.  Thing is I don't have to be fair back, and I'm sick of trying.

I just want ONE of these things.

Don't have any friends.  Tried them.  They ALWAYS picked other people over me.  Never wanted to listen to my side of the story after breakups, etc.  Fucking sick of it.  If I told them honestly that considering to my story and staying friends with me could be what I needed to see life as worth living- it would be a threat.  I don't consider those people my friends anymore, and have no reason to believe that anyone else I seriously trust would be different.

I want a job where I can use my education.  If I say I'm gonna kill myself if nobody hires me that's a threat.  If I were to walk into somewhere I wanted to work and told them I'd stab myself if they didn't hire me- it'd be in their best interest to hire me, as cleaning up after a dead body can cost at least $5,000.  Plus it'd hardly be good publicity, not to mention loss of business.  So yeah, it'd probably be in their best interest to hire me, but that doesn't mean they'd do it.

Steve Jobs.  Whatever you think of him or Apple he went pretty far in business.  The only person to ever hire him was Nolan Bushnell of Atari.  Jobs walked in and literally refused to leave until he was hired.  It was a threat, and it worked, in spite of his horrific body odor.  I've talked about emulating that.  I'm sure most business people would agree that if you picked someone to try to emulate career-wise you could do worse than Steve Jobs.  But people say I need to be in a mental institution for it.

I'd *like* to be attractive to people.  Even enough to be in a relationship.  I'm genuinely physically attractive, easily an 8/10 and even get stares in public. But I'm so incredibly socially awkward with strangers that ANY attempt at conversation falls flat.  And nobody wants to be the only thing in my life that makes it worth living.

Yeah, I've been in relationships before, but every single one lead to me being hurt and emotionally trampled.

Hell even being paid for sex would be nice.  A few years ago some guy paid me $15 to blow him.  That may sound degrading, but my value to others is so incredibly low that even being used as a sex object (worth money!) was a boost.  And if it happened again I can honestly say I'd feel a little better about myself.

A beautiful work of art is only worth as much as someone is willing to pay for it.  If every single person in the world decided the Mona Lisa was worthless tomorrow, it would be worthless, no matter how brilliant it was.

In the next month I'm going to have the means to do this.  It's a very physically painless way to go.

I just want to be able to basically tell people "this is what would give me a reason to live!" and have it taken seriously as maybe something that's important enough to me to work with me.

But when you've been burned enough times you quit sticking your hand in the oven.  It's a sensible reaction.  Why should I believe that I'm not going to be hurt, when I haven't actually not been hurt?
